section.para: The ngx_http_db_module module (1.31.6) retrieves values for the specified key from a database and returns them as HTTP response bodies. The key can contain variables. Authentication and database selection are also supported.
Currently, the module supports single-key lookups using the GET command of Redis database over TCP or TLS.
Lookup results can be cached in a shared memory zone. Retrieved values can be used in variables.

para.note: This module is available as part of our commercial subscription.

section.name: Example Configuration

directive.name: db_auth
directive.para: For the Redis backend, the password is passed as a single argument to the AUTH command.
The directive is inherited from the previous configuration level if and only if there are no db_auth directives defined on the current level.
To protect the password, enable SSL/TLS connections to the database server using the directive.

directive.name: db_bind
directive.para:
Makes outgoing connections to a database server originate from the specified local IP address with an optional port. Parameter value can contain variables. The special value off cancels the effect of the db_bind directive inherited from the previous configuration level, which allows the system to auto-assign the local IP address and port. Example:
db_bind $server_addr;

directive.name: db_buffer_size
directive.para: Sets the size of the buffer used for reading the database response. By default, the buffer size is equal to one memory page. This is either 4K or 8K, depending on a platform. It can be made smaller, however.
The buffer is also used when parsing database protocol replies. A protocol reply header that does not fit in the buffer cannot be processed successfully.
Database response bodies are processed without upstream response buffering.

directive.name: db_cache
directive.para: Enables caching of database lookup results in a shared memory zone defined by the directive. The cache key is the value of the directive, evaluated for the current request. If a cached result is found, it is returned without connecting to the database server.
The directive must be specified in the same configuration context.

The following parameters are supported:
timeout=time
sets the lifetime of cached values. The parameter defaults to 0. A nonzero effective timeout should be configured using this parameter or the zone's timeout parameter. With an effective timeout of zero, entries may be removed by unrelated writes to the zone.
max_size=size
sets the maximum value size eligible for caching. By default, the size is 64k. Values exceeding this limit are returned to the client but are not cached.
not_found=off | on | time
Enables or disables caching of not found results. By default, such results are not cached. The value on uses the same timeout as for database values. A time value specifies a separate lifetime for not found results.

The evaluated value is used as the cache key. A cached value is returned without contacting the database. A cached missing-key result returns
if missing-key caching is enabled in the current location. Otherwise, the database is queried.

A zero-length value is a successful result and is distinct from a missing key. Only complete, valid successful responses are cached, together with missing-key results when enabled. Failed, malformed, or incomplete responses are not cached.
Locations sharing a zone must have identical , , and settings. A cache zone must not also be used for ordinary keyval data. Missing-key caching cannot be combined with the not_found parameter of .
A cache lookup error returns . Failure to insert a result into the cache does not affect the response.
The directive is inherited from the previous configuration level unless overridden.

para.note: The module does not provide cache invalidation or purge. Database changes may remain invisible until cached entries expire or are evicted. Concurrent cache misses are not combined into a single database request.

directive.name: db_connect_timeout
directive.para: Defines a timeout for establishing a connection with a database server. It should be noted that this timeout cannot usually exceed 75 seconds.

directive.name: db_get
directive.para: Specifies the key to retrieve from the database. The key can contain text, variables, and their combination. An empty key is not allowed.
If caching is enabled, the evaluated key is also used as the cache key.

directive.name: db_name
directive.para: Sets the database to use for lookup requests.

directive.name: db_next_upstream
directive.para: One should bear in mind that passing a request to the next server is only possible if nothing has been sent to a client yet. That is, if an error or timeout occurs in the middle of the transferring of a response, fixing this is impossible.

The directive also defines what is considered an unsuccessful attempt of communication with a server. The cases of error and timeout, are always considered unsuccessful attempts, even if they are not specified in the directive. The case of invalid_response is considered an unsuccessful attempt only if it is specified in the directive. The case of not_found is never considered an unsuccessful attempt.
Passing a request to the next server can be limited by the number of tries and by time.
The not_found parameter cannot be combined with enabled missing-key caching in .

directive.name: db_next_upstream_timeout
directive.para: Limits the time during which a request can be passed to the next server. The 0 value turns off this limitation.

directive.name: db_next_upstream_tries
directive.para: Limits the number of possible tries for passing a request to the next server. The limit includes the initial attempt. The 0 value turns off this limitation.

directive.name: db_pass
directive.para: The directive must also be configured, either in the current configuration or inherited from a parent location.
Only GET and HEAD requests are accepted. Other methods return . The client request body is discarded. Client headers and the request body are not forwarded to the database.

The response content type is determined by the and
directives.

directive.name: db_read_timeout
directive.para: Defines a timeout for reading data from a database server. The timeout is set only between two successive read operations, not for the transmission of the whole response. If the database server does not transmit anything within this time, the connection is closed.

directive.name: db_send_timeout
directive.para: Defines a timeout for sending data to a database server.

directive.name: db_socket_keepalive
directive.para: Configures the “TCP keepalive” behavior for outgoing connections to a database server. If enabled, the SO_KEEPALIVE socket option is turned on.
This is distinct from caching idle upstream connections, which is configured using the directive.

directive.name: db_ssl
directive.para: Enables TLS for connections to database servers.

para.note: Server certificate verification is disabled by default. Verification is configured separately by .

directive.name: db_ssl_certificate
directive.para: Specifies a file with the certificate in the PEM format used for authentication to a database server. The corresponding must also be configured.

The parameter value can contain variables:
db_ssl_certificate /etc/nginx/client-certs/$host.crt;

directive.name: db_ssl_certificate_cache
directive.para: Defines a cache that stores SSL certificates and secret keys specified with variables.

Example:
db_ssl_certificate_cache max=1000 inactive=20s valid=1m;

directive.name: db_ssl_certificate_key
directive.para: Specifies a file with the secret key in the PEM format for the certificate configured by the directive.

The parameter value can contain variables:
db_ssl_certificate_key /etc/nginx/client-certs/$host.key;

directive.name: db_ssl_ciphers
directive.para: Specifies the enabled ciphers for connections to database servers. The ciphers are specified in the format understood by the OpenSSL library.

directive.name: db_ssl_conf_command
directive.para: Sets arbitrary OpenSSL configuration commands when establishing a connection with the database server.

Several db_ssl_conf_command directives can be specified on the same level. These directives are inherited from the previous configuration level if and only if there are no db_ssl_conf_command directives defined on the current level.

para.note: Note that configuring OpenSSL directly might result in unexpected behavior.

directive.name: db_ssl_crl
directive.para: Specifies a file with revoked certificates (CRL) in the PEM format used to verify the certificate of the database server. When using intermediate certificates, their CRLs should be specified in the same file.

directive.name: db_ssl_key_log
directive.para: Enables logging of database server connection SSL keys and specifies the path to the key log file. Keys are logged in the SSLKEYLOGFILE format compatible with Wireshark.

para.note: TLS key logs contain sensitive material that can enable decryption of captured traffic. Protect these files and enable logging only when needed.

directive.name: db_ssl_name
directive.para: Allows overriding the server name used to verify the database server certificate and to be passed through SNI when establishing a connection with the database server.

directive.name: db_ssl_password_file
directive.para: Specifies a file with passphrases for secret keys where each passphrase is specified on a separate line. Passphrases are tried in turn when loading the key.

directive.name: db_ssl_protocols
directive.para: Enables the specified protocols for connections to database servers.

directive.name: db_ssl_server_name
directive.para: Enables or disables passing of the server name through TLS Server Name Indication extension (SNI, RFC 6066) when establishing a connection with the database server.

directive.name: db_ssl_session_reuse
directive.para: Determines whether SSL sessions can be reused when working with the database server. If the errors “digest check failed” appear in the logs, try disabling session reuse.

directive.name: db_ssl_trusted_certificate
directive.para: Specifies a file with trusted CA certificates in the PEM format used to verify the certificate of the database server.

directive.name: db_ssl_verify
directive.para: Enables or disables verification of the database server certificate. The directive must also be configured. The directive is required when is enabled.

directive.name: db_ssl_verify_depth
directive.para: Sets the verification depth in the database server certificate chain. The directive is required when is enabled.

directive.name: db_type
db_var
directive.para: If the subrequest returns the , its response body is assigned to the variable. An empty response body is a valid value.

If the subrequest returns the , the value specified by the default parameter is assigned to the variable. The parameter value can contain variables. If no default parameter is specified, the variable is marked as not found.

Variables are populated during the pre-access phase, not when first evaluated. They should be consumed in subsequent processing phases, such as access or content processing. Reading them earlier, for example in rewrite-phase , , or processing, does not initiate a lookup.
